fieldValues.title: Ctrl-Enter splits a paragraph at the caret, and Ctrl-Z joins it again
fieldValues.move: While editing a paragraph in the essay editor, Ctrl-Enter (Cmd-Enter on a Mac) keeps the text before the caret and moves the rest into a new paragraph directly after it, with the caret at its start. The split is one step in the writer's undo history (SP-89), so Ctrl-Z joins the paragraph again. At the end of a paragraph Ctrl-Enter still adds an empty paragraph.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: Splitting a pasted draft automatically at its blank lines, or importing a document file. The paragraph's title, comments and attachments stay with the first half.
fieldValues.falsifier: The writer splits a pasted draft and text is lost or reordered, or Ctrl-Z after a split does not restore the paragraph as it was.
fieldValues.return_when: After the first essay drafted elsewhere has been pasted in and split, or the first time a split loses text.
